events.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) expected to miss the next few weeks; TreVeyon Henderson still out ill
events.detail: Stevenson has a plantaris tendon issue in the back of his knee from the 45-27 loss to Green Bay; it needs no surgery, only rest and rehab, and should cost the next few weeks, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. TreVeyon Henderson has missed two games with an illness, so Corey Kiner and Lan Larison could be the top two backs against Detroit in Munich. A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) has missed two games; the team plans for him to travel to Germany with no decision made. Stevenson leads the team with 399 rushing yards on 102 carries.
events.so_what: Stevenson is a bench for at least Week 10 and likely beyond. The vacancy does not make Henderson a hold by itself: his neurological illness has no diagnosis or timeline, so his value turns on a return to practice, not on the depth chart. Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are deep-league fliers only until a Week 10 split is clear. Brown stays a week-to-week watch.

source.label: NBC Sports/PFT: Stevenson will miss multiple weeks (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Gardner Minshew (torn UCL, throwing arm) likely needs season-ending surgery; Carson Beck in line to start for Arizona
events.detail: Minshew is seeking additional opinions but will likely need season-ending surgery on a torn UCL in his throwing arm, per NFL.com's Monday roundup, which says Carson Beck is in line to start. Arizona also lost Michael Wilson for the season to a neck fracture and signed Josh Johnson off Cincinnati's practice squad.
events.so_what: Drop Minshew in every format. A rookie starter behind this line lowers the passing floor for Trey McBride, who is now the clear first read with Wilson gone and should still be started on volume. Beck is not a streamer.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Nov. 9

events.headline: Brandon Aiyuk removed from the reserve/left squad list; Mike Evans not expected to practice this week, Deebo Samuel could return Wednesday
events.detail: The 49ers took Aiyuk off the reserve/left squad list, opening a two-week window before he must be added to the 53-man roster, per NFL.com. Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) is not expected to practice this week, while Deebo Samuel (hamstring) could return to practice Wednesday.
events.so_what: Aiyuk is worth a bench stash where he is unrostered, but he is not a Week 10 option. Evans looks like another missed week. Samuel's Wednesday practice status is the tell for whether he is startable Sunday.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Nov. 9

events.headline: Justin Herbert avoids a fracture in his left middle finger; Jim Harbaugh says he should be good to go
events.detail: Herbert hurt the middle finger on his non-throwing hand in the Week 9 loss to Houston. Imaging showed no fracture, and Harbaugh said he should be "good to go" moving forward, per NFL.com. He has not been formally cleared on an injury report.
events.so_what: Start Herbert as usual and watch the midweek report. A non-throwing-hand finger rarely moves passing volume, so his receivers hold their value.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Nov. 9

events.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) day-to-day per Andy Reid ahead of Week 10 at Atlanta
events.detail: Worthy pulled up on a non-contact play late in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets and was ruled out after catching all six targets for 48 yards. On Monday Reid called him day-to-day for Sunday's game at Atlanta, per the Chiefs' official site via RotoWire; no MRI result has been reported. If he is limited, the snaps behind Rashee Rice go to some mix of Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong. Kansas City is reported to be shopping for a receiver before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline.
events.so_what: Day-to-day is a forecast, not a clearance, and hamstrings that end with a player unable to bear weight often linger. Hold him, keep a fallback receiver ready for Week 10, and watch Wednesday's practice report. A receiver added by Kansas City on Tuesday would cut into his targets once he is back.

source.label: RotoWire: Xavier Worthy considered day-to-day, per Reid (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Josh Jacobs fractured his right ring finger and needs surgery; out up to three weeks, IR not ruled out
events.detail: Matt LaFleur said Monday that Jacobs fractured the ring finger on his right hand when it caught a Patriots defender's facemask on a stiff-arm, and that playing through it was not an option because he had no grip strength; the staff tried tape and then a cast Sunday before he was shut down, per ESPN. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported he will be out up to three weeks, and LaFleur did not rule out injured reserve, which would cost at least four games. Kaleb Johnson carried 14 times for 68 yards in the 45-27 win, Pierre Strong Jr. also finished the game, and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) was inactive. Green Bay has been named among the teams that checked in on Jonathan Taylor before Tuesday's deadline.
events.so_what: Jacobs is out for Week 10 and likely longer: move him to IR where the slot allows rather than drop him, since a finger usually heals on schedule. Kaleb Johnson is the back to add and start this week off his 14-carry share, with Strong taking some work; Lloyd returning or a Taylor trade to Green Bay would cap that, so treat Johnson as a short-term volume play.

source.label: ESPN: Packers RB Josh Jacobs needs surgery on finger, IR not ruled out (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) expected to be "full go" Thursday vs. Washington after sitting Week 9
events.detail: John Harbaugh said Monday that Skattebo should be a full go for Thursday night's home game against Washington; he was very close to playing at Philadelphia but the team held him out with a short week ahead, per NBC Sports. Devin Singletary led the backfield in the 19-11 win with Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR. Harbaugh also said J.J. McCarthy (hip pointer) looks like he will play and that the Giants are probably not adding a running back for this game.
events.so_what: Expected to play is still a forecast on a Thursday game, so check the Wednesday estimated report and Thursday's inactives before lineups lock early. If he plays he is back to a full workload start and Singletary returns to the bench. Harbaugh's comment makes a Giants trade for Jonathan Taylor less likely for this week.

source.label: NBC Sports/PFT: Giants expect Cam Skattebo to play on Thursday night (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) in line to miss multiple weeks, per Brian Schottenheimer; out at least Week 10 vs. San Francisco
events.detail: After Monday's imaging, Schottenheimer said Ferguson is in line to miss multiple weeks, which rules him out of the 49ers game and points to a possible IR stint, per RotoWire. He was hurt in the third quarter of the 27-23 win at Indianapolis while already playing through a low ankle sprain. Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) and James Mitchell are next at tight end, and Dallas could add one before Tuesday's deadline. George Pickens (hamstring) and KaVontae Turpin were inactive in Week 9, which pushed Ryan Flournoy into a featured slot role beside CeeDee Lamb.
events.so_what: Ferguson is a multi-week bench or IR stash, not a Sunday decision. Replace him at tight end now; none of the Dallas backups is a startable fill-in. CeeDee Lamb absorbs the short-area targets while Ferguson and Pickens are both down.

source.label: RotoWire: Jake Ferguson in line to miss multiple weeks (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Browns plan to return to Deshaun Watson as the Week 10 starter vs. Houston after Shedeur Sanders' fill-in
events.detail: A source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday that Cleveland will start Watson against the Texans after he cleared concussion protocol. Sanders started Week 9 and completed 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns in a 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. Todd Monken said Monday he was not ready to announce the decision.
events.so_what: Watson is back to a matchup-dependent streaming QB against Houston, and Sanders goes back to the bench. Browns pass catchers keep the same outlook either way; nothing here changes their Week 10 starts.

source.label: ESPN: Browns returning to Watson as QB1 despite Sanders' strong fill-in start (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Sam Darnold (quad, rib) out for Week 10; Drew Lock (oblique) expected to start vs. the Raiders
events.detail: Mike Macdonald said Monday that Darnold, dealing with a quad injury and a broken rib, will miss Week 10 against Las Vegas, which with Seattle's Week 11 bye gives him extra time; he is expected back for the Nov. 29 game at San Francisco, per CBS Sports. Lock hurt his oblique in Sunday's 17-3 win over Arizona on top of elbow tendinitis, but Macdonald said he had a good exam and the injury is something the team can manage. If Lock cannot go, Jalen Milroe, who has not thrown an NFL pass, would start.
events.so_what: Darnold is a hold through the bye, not a Week 10 option. Lock is a low-ceiling streamer on a managed oblique; the bigger effect is on the Seattle pass catchers, who get a week of lower-volume quarterback play. Milroe starting would add rushing value under the konami premium but is not the expected outcome.

source.label: CBS Sports: Seahawks plan to start Drew Lock in Week 10 despite oblique injury (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Puka Nacua headed to IR with MCL and PCL sprains plus turf toe, per Sean McVay
events.detail: Nacua hurt his knee on the Rams' final offensive snap, a jet-sweep handoff, in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington, and had an MRI Monday. The team had said beforehand it did not believe the ACL was torn. McVay told reporters Monday that the Rams expect to place him on injured reserve with MCL and PCL sprains and turf toe, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport; no timeline was given. Injured reserve means at least four games.
events.so_what: Move him to an IR slot rather than drop him; a sprain with no ACL tear is a return-this-season injury. He is out for at least four weeks, so plan the Week 10 to 13 lineups without him and treat the Rams' other receivers as the beneficiaries of a large target vacancy.

source.label: ESPN (Ian Rapoport): Rams expected to place WR Puka Nacua on IR (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Patrick Mahomes (right elbow) day-to-day after a clean MRI; Reid calls it "more positive news than negative"
events.detail: Mahomes hurt his throwing elbow in Sunday's win over the Jets but returned without missing an offensive snap and finished with 242 yards and two touchdowns. An MRI showed no major injury, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, and Reid said Monday it looks like a matter of rehabbing the soreness, per ESPN. Reid did not know whether he would take full reps in practice this week and said the team would see where he is Wednesday. Kansas City plays at Atlanta on Sunday.
events.so_what: Day-to-day after a clean MRI points toward playing, but it is still a forecast on a throwing elbow; keep him in lineups and watch Wednesday's practice participation. A limited week would mostly threaten his passing volume, with Xavier Worthy also day-to-day.

source.label: ESPN: Reid says Mahomes (elbow) day-to-day, news more positive than negative (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Michael Wilson out for the season with a neck fracture he played through in Week 9
events.detail: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Wilson suffered a fracture in his neck area on the fourth play of Sunday's 17-3 loss at Seattle, kept playing, and was diagnosed in tests Monday, per Arizona Sports. He had 51 catches on 89 targets for 546 yards and two touchdowns. Kendrick Bourne is also out, which leaves Trey McBride as the focal point of the passing game; Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded to Houston in October.
events.so_what: Wilson can be dropped in every format. His 89 targets have to go somewhere, and Trey McBride, already the top option, is the clearest gainer; no remaining Arizona receiver has shown enough to justify a waiver bid off this alone.

source.label: Arizona Sports: Cardinals' Michael Wilson out for season with neck injury (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Carson Wentz goes 8-of-25 for 81 yards and two INTs in a 23-6 loss to Buffalo; Kyler Murray (hamstring) still week-to-week
events.detail: Starting for Murray on Monday night, Wentz posted an 8.9 passer rating with two interceptions and a lost fumble before Max Brosmer replaced him in the fourth quarter (6-of-7, 58 yards), per the Vikings' game observations. Both picks came on throws to Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. Jordan Mason had the Vikings' best runs. Murray has a Grade 2 hamstring strain that Kevin O'Connell called week-to-week, and Minnesota has a short week before its trip to Green Bay. No Week 10 starter had been named.
events.so_what: Murray stays a bench for Week 10 and the rushing premium goes with him. Whoever starts, the Minnesota passing game is a downgrade: Jefferson and Hockenson keep volume but the INT risk and stalled drives cap their ceiling. Neither Wentz nor Brosmer is a streaming option. Mason is the back who looked useful.

source.label: Vikings.com: Bills game observations (Nov. 9)

events.headline: Luther Burden III (head) exits Sunday night win over Tampa Bay; Bears have a Week 10 bye
events.detail: Burden caught 7 passes for 97 yards, including a 56-yard first-quarter touchdown from Caleb Williams, before leaving with what appeared to be a head injury; concussion testing was expected, per NBC Sports. He also lost a fumble with 3:38 left that set up Tampa Bay's tying score in a 27-24 Chicago win. Chicago is off in Week 10, so his next game is Week 11 against Detroit.
events.so_what: Not a Week 10 lineup problem because of the bye; he needs to clear the protocol before Week 11. The fumble cost -2 on top of a strong line. Kalif Raymond is the Bears receiver who gains if he misses Week 11, a dart throw at most.

source.label: NBC Sports: Luther Burden exits with head injury vs. Bucs (Nov. 8)

events.headline: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) ruled out at Carolina; Denver has its Week 10 bye
events.detail: Waddle took a shot to the helmet from Panthers rookie safety Zakee Wheatley going up for a deep pass from Bo Nix and was ruled out for the second half with a concussion, per NBC Sports. He had one catch for 22 yards. The Broncos won their fifth straight and are off in Week 10, so his next game is Week 11 and he must clear the protocol, including an independent neurological consultant, first.
events.so_what: Not a Week 10 problem, because Denver is on bye anyway, so there is no reason to drop or panic-bid. Watch his practice reports in the Week 11 run-up. Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant are the Broncos receivers who gain if the protocol drags.

source.label: NBC Sports: Waddle (concussion) ruled out for second half (Nov. 8)

events.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown active at Miami, off the Lions inactive list
events.detail: Detroit's inactives at Miami are Cade Mays, DJ Wonnum, D.J. Reed, Jacob Saylors, Jackson Meeks, Ahmed Hassanein and Mekhi Wingo. St. Brown, questionable with a rib injury after three limited practices, is not among them. Sione Vaki is also active and backs up Jahmyr Gibbs with Saylors out.
events.so_what: Amon-Ra St. Brown is active: start him as a WR1. Jahmyr Gibbs is unaffected; Saylors being out does not change his workload.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Lions, Dolphins Week 9 inactives (Nov. 8)

events.headline: A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson out vs. Green Bay; Hunter Henry active after a questionable tag
events.detail: Friday's final report rules out Brown (ankle, knee) and Henderson (illness). Henry (foot) sat the first two practices, returned limited Friday and was questionable, then was active Sunday per CBS Sports' inactives tracker; rookie Eli Raridon remains the other tight end. Rhamondre Stevenson is not on the report and leads the backfield with Corey Kiner as the spell back. Mack Hollins (calf) came off IR Saturday and is questionable; he led New England in catches and yards when he went down four games ago, per Pro Football Rumors. Henderson said in a Friday statement, per Pro Football Rumors, that he was hospitalized for several days with unexplained neurological symptoms affecting his strength and coordination; there is no return timeline.
events.so_what: Bench Brown. Henderson is an indefinite absence rather than a one-week illness, so he is an IR stash where you have the slot and Stevenson is a confident RB2/FLEX start on volume for the foreseeable future. Henry played on a limited practice week; his Sunday snap share decides whether he is a Week 10 start or a TE to stream around.

source.label: Patriots.com: Patriots rule out A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson; Hunter Henry questionable (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson active vs. Cleveland for his NFL debut after IR activation
events.detail: The Saints activated Tyson Saturday, per RotoWire, and Jordan Schultz reports he intends to make his NFL debut Sunday. He never reached a full practice this week and keeps a questionable tag, so Pro Football Rumors expects a cautious first game. LT Kelvin Banks is also being activated. Travis Etienne Jr.'s window has not opened, CJ Donaldson (shoulder, concussion) is out, Alvin Kamara (back) is cleared, and the Saints waived Kendre Miller. He was active Sunday, per CBS Sports' inactives tracker.
events.so_what: Tyson is a bench-and-watch in his first game back from a season-long hamstring issue; his snap share Sunday decides whether he is a Week 10 start. Donaldson out and Etienne not back leave Kamara and Audric Estime as the backfield, and Estime is a cheap add only if he gets the clear No. 2 role Sunday.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Saints to activate WR Jordyn Tyson, LT Kelvin Banks (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Colts expected to take the best offer for Jonathan Taylor by Tuesday; Giants pulled their bid, Packers and Vikings among suitors
events.detail: Per Pro Football Talk (Nov. 8), league circles expect the 2-7 Colts to accept the best offer for Taylor before the 4 p.m. ET Tuesday deadline; teams linked to him include the Giants, Vikings, Seahawks, Broncos and Packers. ESPN reported Nov. 7 that the Giants pulled a recent offer and that the Colts held a bid of a second-round pick and more while wanting something closer to a first. Josh Downs, who requested a trade, had at least one offer including a fourth; teams have also called about Daniel Jones and Keenan Allen. Tennessee is not trading Tony Pollard but is listening on Calvin Ridley. Jacksonville has fielded calls on Brian Thomas Jr., with Kansas City interested.
events.so_what: Taylor stays a start wherever he lands, but a move into a shared backfield would cut his volume; Green Bay, with Josh Jacobs out after finger surgery, would be the cleanest fit for his workload. Seth McGowan is the Colts back to own the moment a deal is official. Hold Downs and Thomas through Tuesday rather than sell on rumor. Any Jones exit opens Anthony Richardson, whose rushing scores at running-back rates under the konami premium. Pollard staying put keeps him a volume start.

source.label: NBC Sports/PFT: Colts are expected to take best offer for Jonathan Taylor at deadline (Nov. 8)

events.headline: Emeka Egbuka active and played Sunday night at Chicago, his first game since Week 6
events.detail: Egbuka, questionable with a foot injury after full Thursday and Friday practices, played in the 27-24 loss at Chicago and caught 3 of 5 targets for 38 yards, per Bleacher Report's box score. Tez Johnson caught 2 of 5 targets for 76 yards.
events.so_what: The foot held up for a full game, so he is a start again in Week 10 if he practices normally; a quiet return on five targets is not a reason to bench him.

source.label: Bleacher Report: Caleb Williams, Bears top Bucs despite 5 turnovers, box score (Nov. 8)

events.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) placed on IR; Khalil Herbert promoted behind Bijan Robinson
events.detail: Atlanta put Robinson on IR Saturday after he missed two games with a lingering hamstring injury, per ESPN's Marc Raimondi via RotoWire. He must miss at least four more games, with mid-December the earliest return. The Falcons promoted Khalil Herbert from the practice squad as the No. 2 back.
events.so_what: Bijan Robinson's workload was already secure and this removes his only real competition for touches. Brian Robinson Jr. is an IR stash at most; Herbert is a handcuff for Bijan managers only, not a FAAB bid.

source.label: RotoWire: Brian Robinson placed on injured reserve (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Pat Bryant activated from IR but still questionable at Carolina; Sean Payton says he is in line to play
events.detail: Denver activated Bryant Saturday, per RotoWire. He sprained his right ankle and was carted off in Week 4 at San Francisco, went on IR before Week 5, and practiced fully all week after being designated to return Wednesday. He keeps a questionable tag, but Payton told The Denver Gazette on Friday that he expects him to play. Kickoff is 1:00 p.m. ET.
events.so_what: A first game back after five weeks out is a bench-and-watch, not a start. His snap share Sunday decides whether he is worth a Week 10 FLEX look in a Broncos receiver room that has rotated without him.

source.label: RotoWire: Pat Bryant activated from IR (Nov. 7)

events.headline: D.J. Moore and Keon Coleman cleared, no designation for Monday at Minnesota; Joshua Palmer ruled out
events.detail: Moore (shoulder) was limited all week and still wore a non-contact jersey Saturday, as he has since an AC joint sprain in Week 2, but carries no game status, per RotoWire. Coleman (shoulder) is also clear. Palmer (hamstring) will not play. Moore has 16 catches for 260 yards and two touchdowns on 27 targets in five games.
events.so_what: Moore plays and is a FLEX-range receiver against a Minnesota team starting Carson Wentz. Palmer's absence concentrates the targets on Moore, Coleman and the tight ends.

source.label: RotoWire: DJ Moore in clear for Week 9 (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Christian Kirk to IR, Demarcus Robinson activated and cleared; Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel out vs. the Raiders
events.detail: San Francisco placed Kirk on IR with a meniscus injury Saturday and activated Robinson (ankle), who no longer carries a designation, per RotoWire. Evans (Achilles, aggravated in Week 6) misses a third straight game and Samuel (hamstring) is out, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner. The active receivers are Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing. Separately, Brandon Aiyuk met with the 49ers and his agent Friday after filing reinstatement paperwork in late October, saying he is healthy; roughly $13 million in forfeited bonuses could push it to arbitration, and the team could release, trade or roster him, per RotoWire (Nov. 7).
events.so_what: Bench Evans and Samuel. Kirk is out at least four games. The thin receiver room should funnel touches to the backfield and tight end, and no 49ers fill-in receiver is worth a bid on a depleted room. Aiyuk is a speculative stash only where a bench slot is free; nothing is resolved and he may never play for San Francisco.

source.label: 49ers lose WR Christian Kirk to IR; activate WR Demarcus Robinson (Nov. 7)
